findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile per-candidate `InstrumentedModel` wrapping with the already-live `Agent.instrument_all()` (tracing.py:54) so exactly one candidate span is emitted (e.g. document that a wrapped concrete model is not re-instrumented by instrument_all, or gate the wrapper accordingly).
evidence: Plan: 'wrap each already-built concrete candidate model ... with InstrumentedModel ... so each candidate request emits an OpenTelemetry span'
tracing.py:54 Agent.instrument_all() 'emit agent/LLM/tool spans through the configured provider' — already instruments model requests globally when the [tracing] extra + keys are present
AC-1: 'emit one OTel span per attempted candidate, nested beneath the Agent model-request span'
findings.finding: The plan wraps each candidate in InstrumentedModel while `setup_tracing` already calls `Agent.instrument_all()` globally, and does not reconcile the two so that exactly one library span per candidate is emitted rather than duplicate/nested instrumentation spans.
scenarios: Tracing enabled via setup_tracing (instrument_all live) AND candidates wrapped in InstrumentedModel: a single candidate request may be instrumented twice, producing duplicate or doubly-nested spans
InstrumentationSettings on the candidate wrapper conflicts with the provider/settings established by instrument_all

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the raised reason is wrapped under the allowlisted `message` field of the dict handed to `sanitize_diagnostic` (which drops non-allowlisted keys), so the sanitized reason actually lands on the `raised` span.
evidence: failure.py:131-140 `sanitize_diagnostic(fields: dict)` iterates `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` only and skips everything else
failure.py:103 shows `message` is the free-text allowlisted key; a raw string arg is not a dict and would not survive
Plan phrasing 'the raised reason passed through `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic`' does not state the reason is keyed under `message`
findings.finding: The plan says the raised reason is 'passed through' `sanitize_diagnostic`, but that function sanitizes a keyed dict against an allowlist and DROPS any key not in `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`; a bare error string must be placed under the allowlisted `message` key or it will be silently discarded (yielding an empty `raised` span reason).
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('Any error text placed on a `raised` span is passed through the existing `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` allowlist sanitizer') and AC-5
scenarios: A candidate raises with a diagnostic string; executor calls sanitize_diagnostic on the bare string or under a non-allowlisted key; the `raised` span carries no reason
Secret-canary test passes trivially because the reason was dropped, masking a real regression
findings.suggested_fix: State that the candidate wrapper builds `sanitize_diagnostic({"message": <error text>})` and reads back the `message` value onto the span's `outcome=raised` reason attribute, matching the allowlist contract in failure.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete InstrumentedModel/InstrumentationSettings API used to (a) attach rebar attributes (order, outcome, usage) to the emitted span and (b) guarantee nesting under the Agent model-request span, or route a short SPIKE to confirm the span-attribute hook before committing.
evidence: resolve_symbol confirms pydantic_ai.models.instrumented.InstrumentedModel EXISTS (Verified) but the attribute-injection surface is Partially-verified — the specific public hook is unconfirmed from repo-confined tools (.venv is outside the snapshot)

Plan asserts InstrumentedModel 'emit[s] an OpenTelemetry span nested ... beneath the existing Agent model-request span' and that rebar records attributes 'On top of the library span' without naming how attributes are set on a library-owned span
InstrumentationSettings and WrapperModel exist, so the wrapping mechanism is achievable; the unconfirmed piece is the attribute/nesting surface
findings.finding: The plan depends on attaching custom rebar attributes (order, outcome, optional usage) to the span that InstrumentedModel emits internally, but does not name the public API hook that makes this possible — InstrumentedModel manages its own request span lifecycle, and there is no plan-stated mechanism for rebar to inject attributes into it (vs. emitting a separate rebar-owned child span).
findings.location: Approach paragraph: 'On top of the library span, record rebar attributes: zero-based order, provider-qualified model identity, an outcome ...'
scenarios: If InstrumentedModel exposes no public hook to add attributes to its own span, the AC 'each candidate span carries ... order ... outcome' cannot be met on the library span and would require a rebar-owned child span, changing the nesting story
The 'nested beneath the Agent model-request span through ambient span context' claim may not hold if InstrumentedModel starts its span outside the Agent request context

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and state whether a swallowed instrumentation failure emits a minimal non-fatal operator signal (e.g. a single debug/warn log) rather than being fully silent, or document why total silence is the intended tradeoff.
evidence: 'any exception in candidate wrapping or span emission ... is swallowed at the wrapper boundary'
The story's purpose is operational visibility of candidate activity; a silent swallow removes the signal that it failed
findings.finding: Instrumentation failures (candidate wrapping or span emission) are swallowed silently at the wrapper boundary with no operator-visible signal, so a degraded/absent trace — the very visibility this story adds — can occur without any indication.
findings.location: Approach — 'any exception ... is swallowed at the wrapper boundary'
scenarios: A span exporter misconfiguration silently drops all candidate spans and operators believe fallback is not occurring
Candidate wrapping raises for a new provider type and traces silently go missing
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the best-effort swallow of the run path but emit a lightweight, rate-limited warn/debug log at the wrapper boundary when instrumentation raises, so the tracing degradation is diagnosable without affecting result/usage/exception.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the raised reason maps onto `sanitize_diagnostic`'s allowlisted-dict contract (failure.py:131) — name the allowlisted key the reason travels under, or introduce a string-level redaction path (`_redact`) if the reason is free-form.
evidence: Plan: 'Any error text placed on a `raised` span is passed through the existing `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` allowlist sanitizer'
failure.py:131 def sanitize_diagnostic(fields: dict) -> dict: iterates _ALLOWED_FIELDS and drops unknown keys; only string VALUES are redacted
findings.finding: The plan routes raised error text through `sanitize_diagnostic`, but that function takes a dict of allowlisted KEYS and drops unknown keys — it does not sanitize a free-form string — so the plan's usage is a signature mismatch and never names which allowlisted key carries the raised reason.
findings.location: Approach ('error text placed on a raised span is passed through ... sanitize_diagnostic'); failure.py:131-140
scenarios: Implementer passes a raw exception message as a value under a key not in _ALLOWED_FIELDS: the reason is silently dropped from the span
Implementer bypasses the allowlist to keep the reason, defeating the secret-canary AC

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel-wrapped candidates preserve the per-candidate `.profile`, `.model_name`, and `.models` reads that `capabilities_for` (capabilities.py:449) and `_check_tool_capability` (runner.py:726) depend on — e.g. resolve capabilities/tool-capability over the CONCRETE models before wrapping, or confirm WrapperModel proxies these attributes.
evidence: Plan: 'wrap concrete candidate models with InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel at construction, without changing order or fallback predicates'
runner.py:408-411 iterates getattr(model, 'models', [model]) and calls _check_tool_capability(candidate_model, candidate)
runner.py:431: _intersect_capabilities([capabilities_for(m) for m in model.models])
capabilities_for (capabilities.py:449-452) reads getattr(model, 'profile') and getattr(model, 'model_name'); a None profile silently degrades to the conservative record
_check_tool_capability (runner.py:726) reads getattr(getattr(model, 'profile', None), 'supports_tools', None)
findings.finding: Wrapping each concrete candidate in InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel interposes a proxy in front of the profile-reading seams the runner drives per candidate, and the plan does not state how the wrapper preserves .profile/.model_name/.models pass-through that capability resolution depends on.
findings.location: Approach / Scope (model_classes.py candidate wrapping); runner.py:408-411,431; capabilities.py:449-452; runner.py:726
scenarios: A fallback chain where each candidate is now an InstrumentedModel: capabilities_for reads the wrapper's profile; if the wrapper does not proxy .profile/.model_name, capability intersection, prompt-cache style, native-output-under-thinking, and tool-capability fail-fast silently change
model.models used at runner.py:431 now yields wrappers, so _intersect_capabilities and the tool-capability loop operate over wrapped objects
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `_check_tool_capability` and `_intersect_capabilities` over the concrete candidate models (as built today) and wrap only afterward, so the wrapper never sits between the runner and the profile/model_name it reads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the doc that records the candidate-span attribute contract (order, outcome vocabulary, optional-usage semantics) — e.g. an ADR or an AGENTS.md/tracing design-doc update — in Scope.

'the approved RP-01 decision' is referenced but no ADR/design-doc update is listed in Scope

findings.finding: The plan defines a new durable candidate-span attribute contract (zero-based `order`, provider-qualified model identity, closed `outcome` vocabulary {returned,raised}, optional provider-reported usage) that downstream trace consumers/dashboards may depend on, but no scope bullet names an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update capturing this vocabulary as a decision.
scenarios: A future dashboard or trace consumer reads candidate spans and needs to know the stable meaning of `outcome`/`order`
A later story adds a third outcome value and no doc records that the vocabulary was intentionally closed
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope bullet capturing the RP-01 candidate-tracing attribute vocabulary (order/outcome/optional-usage) in an ADR or tracing design-doc so downstream trace consumers have a stable reference.
